q1_issues.issue: Both arguments are bare kind-denoting NPs ('spring tides', 'salt-bloom'), which is the stated trigger for a kind-level relational generic ((Bloom spring_tide salt_bloom), explicitly 'not a per-instance rule'), yet the parse emits the distributing per-instance Implication.

q2_gaps: a bare-kind relational generic that also carries an oblique ('in the tide-pools'): the kind-level relation is an opaque two-argument atom with no slot for a locative, and the instruction set never says which form wins when the relational-generic trigger fires on a clause with obliques
notes: Everything else matches the instruction set: genus-only decomposition of the three noun-modifier compounds, the definite plural as a top-level group witness referenced from inside the rule (the 'Foxes rarely cross the causeway' shape), a bare class symbol for the non-specific object, 0.9/0.9 for the bare generic, and no tense atom.
